subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When structuring a composition, why might a composer reuse a melodic idea in a contrasting section?
options: To create unity while still providing variety
questions.explain: Reusing ideas in new contexts gives a piece unity while contrast keeps it interesting.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'accent' (>) tells a performer to:
options: Hold the note longer than written
questions.explain: An accent mark instructs the player to stress or emphasise that note.

questions.q: A major triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A major triad stacks a major 3rd then a minor 3rd, giving a bright sound.

questions.q: How many beats does a dotted minim last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A dot adds half the note's value, so a minim (2 beats) plus its dot (1 beat) lasts three beats.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: 'Imitation' as a way of developing an idea means:
options: One part copies a melodic idea just stated by another part
questions.explain: Imitation is when one part copies a melodic idea introduced by another part.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'staccato' tells a player to make notes:
questions.explain: Staccato means short and detached, the opposite of legato.

questions.q: Which clef is also known as the G clef and is used for higher-pitched instruments?
questions.explain: The treble (G) clef curls around the G line and is used for higher pitches.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which chord progression?
questions.explain: A perfect cadence moves from chord V to chord I, sounding finished.

questions.q: What does the term 'tutti' instruct in an orchestral score?
questions.explain: Tutti means 'all', instructing the whole ensemble to play together.

questions.q: What does a 'crescendo' instruct a performer to do?
questions.explain: A crescendo is a gradual increase in volume, opposite to a diminuendo.

questions.q: A rondo form is best described by which pattern?
questions.explain: In rondo form a main theme (A) returns between contrasting episodes, e.g. ABACA.

questions.q: How many beats does a crotchet last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A crotchet lasts one beat in 4/4 time.

questions.q: What does 'a tempo' mean after a passage that has slowed down?
questions.explain: 'A tempo' instructs the performer to return to the original speed after a change.

questions.q: When performing in an ensemble, watching a conductor or leader mainly helps players to:
options: Stay together in time and respond to changes
questions.explain: Following a conductor or leader keeps the ensemble together in time and unified in expression.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is a:
questions.explain: C up to G spans five letter names, making a perfect 5th.

questions.q: Which cadence creates a surprise by moving from chord V to chord VI instead of I?
questions.explain: An interrupted cadence moves from V to VI, surprising the listener who expects a perfect cadence.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.

questions.q: A minim is worth how many crotchet beats?
questions.explain: A minim is worth two crotchet beats.

questions.q: The tempo marking 'andante' indicates a speed that is:
questions.explain: Andante means at a walking pace, a moderate tempo between slow and fast.

questions.q: A 'pedal' (or pedal point) in texture is:
options: A sustained or repeated note, often in the bass, held under changing harmonies
questions.explain: A pedal is a held or repeated note, usually in the bass, that continues while harmonies change above it.

questions.q: Which note value lasts the longest?
questions.explain: A semibreve lasts four beats in 4/4, longer than a minim, crotchet or quaver.
